A chart becomes harder to read the moment your ego decides what it should say.

Trading becomes a much simpler game when you separate four things: 1. What you control: selection. 2. What you define: risk. 3. What you execute: the trade. 4. What you can’t control: the outcome. A lot of trading stress comes from trying to control #4 instead of mastering the first three.

Profitable traders spend an incredible amount of time doing things that don't look profitable short term. Reading. Research. Backtesting. Studying charts. Building watchlists. Reviewing trades. Thinking. Waiting. Trading is unusual because some of your most valuable work happens when no capital is moving in the markets.

The secret to trading may be weak competition. Don't compete with algorithms at milliseconds. Don't compete with market makers on spreads. Don't compete with analysts on earnings models. Find the part of the game where your temperament, timeframe, and skills give you an advantage. You don't have to beat everyone. You just have to choose the right game in the market you can win.
